key_insight: SABER directly aligns LLM-derived semantic information with brain network representations, using it to guide diagnosis rather than treating it as a passive add-on.
clinical_relevance: The framework aims to improve brain disease classification robustness, stability, and interpretability, especially when labeled data are limited.
method: ROI-level semantics are fused with brain nodes via global self-attention to add whole-brain context.
Multi-scale hypergraphs model functional subnetworks and higher-order multi-ROI interactions.
A decision-level semantic alignment step injects patient-specific text embeddings into graph representations for prediction.
evidence_signal: On ABIDE and ADHD-200, the method reports state-of-the-art performance, better stability, and improved interpretability, with particular gains in small-sample settings.
watch_item: Performance appears promising, but the approach depends on how well LLM-generated semantics generalize and align with each patient’s brain data in real-world settings.
paper_title: SABER: A Semantic-Aligned Brain Network Analysis Framework via Multi-scale Hypergraphs
